Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comment: There is an explicit marker for the absolutive case.
curated_comment: Pitu Ulunna Salu (filed under bamb1270 = Bambam, ISO ptu, Austronesian, Sulawesi, Indonesia) shows a split-ergative system in which only bound pronouns carry ergative-absolutive marking; free pronouns and full NPs have no morphological case marking and use pronominal indexing on the verb instead. GB409_1=1 (absolutive marker present in pronominal system), GB409_2-4=1 (bound pronouns: distinct A-form [ergative] and S/P-form [absolutive]), GB409_5=0 (full NPs: no case marking, only verb agreement). GB409_6-19=0 (no ergative in these tense/aspect/mood/animacy/topicality contexts because the split is NP-type-based, not conditioned by these factors). GB409_20-21=1 (main and non-main clauses show pronominal ergativity). GB409_22=1 (split conditioned by NP type: pronouns vs. full NPs). GB409_23=1 (ergative = genitive in pronominal forms). Source: Campbell (1989). NOTE: the file uses glottocode bamb1270 (Bambam) but the documented language is Pitu Ulunna Salu; the correct Glottolog code for Pitu Ulunna Salu is pitu1237 (pitu1241, the previously proposed code, does not exist). Researcher should verify whether to keep bamb1270 or change to pitu1237.

Feature: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comment: Ergative marking is conditioned by the nature of NP. Specifically, the system is one of split ergativity: the ergative-absolutive marking occurs only in bound pronouns and free pronouns have no morphological case marking.

Feature: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
